subject: Bluepine subprocessor intake: export constraints & checklist
messages:
From: Bluepine Security Team <security@bluepine.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor inventory + export constraints for EU/UK traffic

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We have a short window before procurement signs off and need a consolidated view of any third-party subprocessors that will process Bluepine data (customer IDs, logs, telemetry) for EU/UK traffic. In particular we need:

- A single-sheet inventory listing subprocessors, country of processing, and whether data leaves the EU/UK.
- Any onshore fallback options (on-prem or EU-only partners) you can commit to during contract negotiation.
- Any technical mitigations (encryption at rest/transit, key custody, tokenization) and a pointer to KMS/HSM controls.

We also need to confirm whether export controls could apply for certain telemetry blobs (our legal flagged a potential export classification). A quick note on timelines: procurement hopes to finalize DPA amendments by EOD Friday. Can you get an initial inventory + a short call?

Best,
Ellen Ruiz
Security / Bluepine Systems
ellen.ruiz@bluepine.com

Attachment: BLUE-82_PCI-questionnaire.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory + export constraints for EU/UK traffic

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clarity and the deadline.

Short answer first: we can provide an export-aware inventory and two onshore options for EU/UK traffic (1) EU-dedicated telemetry routing via our EU edge partners and (2) a Reserved Dedicated lane: Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1 with toggled egress controls. Both are available as contract options; I'll flag costs separately.

I attached an initial inventory (redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v1.csv) and a simple dataflow sketch showing where logs and telemetry may transit. High level notes:
- Core inference models: hosted in multi-region, model weights are static but inference is run on regional pools. EU production traffic can be pinned to eu-cluster variants.
- Observability/metrics: we use StreamPulse (US) by default but can route EU metrics to EdgeMeter (Frankfurt) for customers requiring onshore retention.
- Audit logs + backups: retained in S3-like storage; encryption with customer-specific CMKs is supported for Dedicated/Private customers.

Questions for you:
1) When you say "export classification on telemetry blobs" — can you share an example field or schema so we can confirm whether it contains export-control-relevant identifiers?
2) Would Bluepine accept an amendment that restricts analytics/telemetry to EU partners for the first 12 months with a rollback clause?

I'll loop Rishi and Kimberly for technical and contractual confirmation. Happy to set a 30-min call this afternoon if that's easier.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_v1.csv (csv stub), dataflow_sketch_bluepine_20270614.png (image stub)

Ellen / Marissa — quick technical add:

- Telemetry schema: if any telemetry includes device-level geographic identifiers or raw IP-derived location hashes that Bluepine considers export-controlled, we can add a pre-ingest redaction hook at the EU edge (strip or hash those fields before any US-bound services see them).
- Onshore options: 1) EdgeMeter (Frankfurt) routing is straightforward and supports EU KMS with customer-owned keys. 2) Redwood Dedicated (eu-west-1) will ensure compute + storage stays in-region; backups can be configured to stay in region for the retention window.
- Encryption: we support customer-managed CMKs via our KMS integration (we can supply attestation screenshots for KMS key policy and key origin).

Operational note: the onshore telemetry routing is a configuration flag (no code change) but requires 48–72 hours of provisioning for a Dedicated lane. If procurement needs a hard date in the contract, please add a 10-business-day provisioning SLA for Dedicated.

I'll prepare a short technical appendix if you want a single-page addendum for the DPA that lists the exact controls and provisioning timelines.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Ellen — appreciate the heads-up and the specificity. A few legal/contract items to close out quickly so procurement can finish the DPA amendment this week: 

1) Narrow scoping language: we can amend the DPA to require EU-only processing for the telemetry categories you specify for the first 12 months and include a roll-forward notice period before any cross-border change. Please send a short list of the telemetry fields you require to be restricted.

2) Attachment evidence: Marissa/Rishi — please provide (a) KMS attestation screenshots or procedure, (b) a redacted sample entry of the telemetry schema (so Bluepine's export review team can validate), and (c) a short service-level provisioning timeline that procurement can include.

3) DocuSign amendment: procurement asked for a pre-signed DPA amendment template that they can redline. I'm sharing a DocuSign draft (link below). Once Bluepine confirms restricted fields, Legal can lock the clause and Marissa can present the provisioning SLA.

Next steps I propose:
- Ellen: confirm 3–5 telemetry fields to be held in-region.
- Marissa: send the CSV as a flattened inventory (columns: subprocessor, role, country, EU residency boolean, data types) — your current CSV looks good but procurement wants flattened columns.
- Rishi: produce the one-page tech appendix and the provisioning SLA.

If we can hit those by EOD Thursday, Procurement can accept the amendment and we can close the thread. If needed, we'll offer a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00–10:30am BST.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
